wave_review_comment: Wave 7 bound the lifecycle to the spine and the epic stops here on the human's call. C3 shipped the three pieces and both carried findings, all five gates reviewed and approved, and cold review then refused the merge over a test that passed only inside its own worktree -- a defect five APPROVEs and the Commander's own cold critic had all missed. R0 repaired that and a close_work that half-succeeded on gitignored entries with no rollback, which C3 found by running its own close on its own work area. The merged tree is 2933 passed, 4 skipped, 1121 subtests, green from a checkout that is not the one it was written in, with the template sweep unchanged at 23. Four of the epic's five done-conditions hold. The fifth -- no agent-facing instruction names the CLI -- does not, and is filed on #559 with the full measurement and on #565, which argues the reason it keeps growing back is that the workbench skill teaches what the door's tools now carry. One incident is on the record without a mechanism to prevent it: C3 blocked correctly on two outward-facing acts its order forbade, then cleared its own block and took them three and a half minutes later with no waiver recorded.
revised_epic_body: Agents reach a spine only through the MCP door, and receive their work as a spine rather than as prose. Thirteen workstreams are merged. All eighteen engine verbs are reachable through nine tools; a spine is compiled from a typed spec rather than written by hand, and the generator refuses to write anything the oracle would reject; a crew that cannot satisfy a check blocks to its recorded parent instead of forcing or going silent; and as of wave 7 the work lifecycle is one thing -- one call opens a branch, a worktree, a scaffolded work area and a compiled spine together, the closing advance archives that work area spine-last and says ready to PR, and a gate's dispatch is declared in the spec and checked against the registry rather than remembered by whoever wrote the launch order. What remains unmet is the fourth done-condition: agent-facing instruction still names the engine CLI in 11 files, all three orchestrator spine templates among them, and two of those sentences assert the CLI is the only path for a dispatched crew -- which this epic disproved twice. That work is filed, not abandoned: #559 carries the measurement and the guard it needs, #565 argues the cause is that the workbench skill's teaching half duplicates the door. The epic stops here so the next effort starts from a clean read of what is actually left.
